compression_factor.note: Only the slow ground-settlement process is time-compressed (240 s stands for 24 h at 360x, a PLACEHOLDER label); IMU noise, piezo vibration, LiDAR sweeps, packet loss, and 5 s windows run in uncompressed 1x sensor time.

literature_table.literature_basis_and_sources: Ashton Underground longwall end-of-panel reports (Yancoal, SCT Operations, 2008-2012): measured maximum tilts of about 13 to 103 mm/m (about 0.7 to 5.9 deg; 1 mm/m = 0.0573 deg), with some predictions higher.
literature_table.assessment_or_scope_note: The main range covers the lower half of real longwall maximum tilts; treat it as an early-warning range.

literature_table.literature_basis_and_sources: Jeran and Trevits, US Bureau of Mines RI 9552: most movement within about 30 days of undermining in one study, total duration about a year in the northern Appalachian basin. Colorado DRMS rule document: about 15% of $S_{\max}$ at the face, 5 to 9% residual afterwards. Sustainability 2020, 12(4), 1528: active period defined as above 1.7 mm/day. Standard form is the Knothe time function with coefficient $c$ (Zhang et al., Scientific Reports 12:18433, 2022; Hejmanowski 2015, Int J Coal Sci Technol).
literature_table.assessment_or_scope_note: The smoothstep S-curve is a simplification.

timescale_note: In the frozen simulator configuration, a gradual or normal run is 240 s of sensor time standing for 24 h of the slow ground process (PLACEHOLDER compression factor 360), whereas cited gradual longwall subsidence develops over weeks to months (most movement within about 30 days of undermining in Jeran and Trevits, USBM RI 9552). Using a rough real-world order-of-magnitude reference (DERIVED, ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, not a cited value): about 60 mm/m (3.4 deg) developing over about 30 days gives an average tilt rate of about 0.1 deg/day, whereas compressing the full rise into a fraction of a single 24 h (1-day) run produces much higher implied deg/day rates (audited across all frozen gradual runs in docs/report_literature_checks.md). Replacing the 360x compression label ("24 h per run") with a 30-day compression factor (for example 10,000x to 30,000x) changes only the labelled physical duration and the Definition A (slow-process time) false-alarm-per-hour figure; it does not change the simulated sensor data, window features, or any model score.
